ov: About 75 species of long-legged, long-necked wading birds of fresh water and coasts, including the egrets and bitterns. They fly with the neck pulled back, unlike storks and cranes.

cf.tip: A heron flies with its neck pulled back into an S; a crane flies with its neck stretched out.

fx: Herons have “powder down”, special feathers that crumble into a powder they use to clean off fish slime.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact (some herons drop bait and wait) is confirmed: little egrets and grey herons have been documented using bait.
